description: Machine routing table for AES-V2.5 (SUE-563). Layer ids are the routing target vocabulary fixed by docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5. Prose contract: editorial/FEEDBACK-ROUTING.md. Engine: scripts/lib/routing-core.mjs. This table routes INTO schemas/feedback-record.schema.json's routing.layer / routing.modality_layer / scope fields; it does not redefine them.

shared.owns: The editorial intent was extracted wrongly from the natural-language request: the wrong transformation, content type, audience, surface, or artifact axis was inferred, or a confirmed value was silently overwritten by an assumption.
symptoms: output answers a different transformation than the one requested
an axis is recorded assumed where the human actually confirmed it
a missing_material field was treated as safe to infer instead of raising clarification
the artifact axis (e.g. thumbnail vs body infographic) was read as a style request
shared.repair: Correct the axis value on the Editorial Intent record for this task. If the same phrasing pattern misclassifies repeatedly, that pattern becomes calibration evidence for the intake heuristics — never a same-task prompt patch pretending to be a fix.

do_not.note: An intake misread (wrong artifact or transformation axis) is not the same failure as a correctly-extracted intent applied to the wrong audience profile. Fix the axis that was actually misread.

shared.owns: The wrong reference was selected for craft evidence, or a selected reference was misread — treated as more applicable, more authoritative, or more current than its evaluation supports.
symptoms: the reference is topically on-subject but visually or structurally nothing like what the surface actually publishes
a reference evaluation's applicable_to scope was ignored when the reference was selected
a reference was used as if it were a source (it dictated a fact, not a craft choice)
the same mismatch recurs for one content type or artifact class
shared.repair: Append or correct a reference evaluation record under the validated protocol (references/REFERENCE-EVALUATION-PROTOCOL.md). This is the shared layer whose own default automatic repair already sits at class 2 — appending evaluation metadata is the normal fix, not an exception to it.

do_not.note: A reference-selection failure must not become a content rule. Fixing the lookup that picked a bad reference is a reference-layer repair; writing a new prose rule to compensate for a bad reference is how the system accumulates rules for a lookup bug — see docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, misroute 3.

shared.owns: Audience fit was misjudged: depth, jargon tolerance, purpose framing, or attention budget did not match the profile the intent actually named.
symptoms: explanation depth does not match the audience profile's domain-expertise trait
jargon is unglossed for a beginner-learner or glossed unnecessarily for a domain-expert
the output resolves a different decision than the audience's purpose/decision context calls for
length or segment granularity ignores the audience's attention-context trait
shared.repair: Re-run generation against the correct audience profile trait for this task. A repeated mismatch for one audience profile across tasks is calibration evidence for that profile, not a per-task rewrite.

do_not.note: An audience-fit miss is about who the piece is for, not whether the thesis is worth arguing. Do not rewrite the argument to fix a depth or jargon mismatch.

shared.owns: Thesis, argument path, or article-worthiness: no falsifiable position, a position the piece does not actually argue, or source order standing in for an argument.
symptoms: no sentence carries a falsifiable thesis
the piece could be replaced by reading the sources in order
headings walk the source or repository topology component by component
the strongest counterargument is absent or answered only in a token paragraph
the piece reads correctly but demonstrates coverage instead of deciding what the reader needs
shared.repair: Re-frame: state or restate the thesis and argument path before any prose is regenerated. This is the layer `frame-article` and the HITL `frame` stage exist to catch — see editorial/HITL-PROTOCOL.md.

do_not.note: A frame failure repaired in polish leaves the argument wrong while making it read better. This is the misroute docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5 names first.

shared.owns: Factual support, freshness, or provenance: an unsupported material claim, an interpretation presented as verified, a stale time-sensitive claim, or a citation that resolves but does not support.
symptoms: a citation resolves but does not support the claim beside it
an interpretation is marked or treated as a verified fact
a time-sensitive claim rests on a stale source
a material fact changed after a verification review with no re-verification recorded
shared.repair: Route to verify-claims. A material correction after verification forces a new verification review per editorial/HITL-PROTOCOL.md — polish or any other stage may report the problem but may not fix it.

do_not.note: Polish may not resolve a factual problem by rewording around it; that is a verification-layer finding wearing a prose fix.

shared.owns: Publication or destination constraint: the output does not fit the surface it targets — length, format, materialization, or a publication-profile rule.
symptoms: the artifact violates a surface-specific constraint (length ceiling, format, renderer target)
the output would need reformatting before it could reach its declared surface
a surface-specific rule was applied to the wrong surface
shared.repair: Fix the per-task materialization for this surface. A durable surface rule change is a publication-profile edit — class 5, evidence-backed review — never an automatic escalation from one task.

do_not.note: A one-off surface mismatch is not evidence that the evaluator or the active calibration snapshot is wrong; it is evidence about this task's materialization.

shared.owns: The evaluator's judgement was wrong, or the currently active calibration snapshot itself no longer matches owner preference.
symptoms: repeated independent evidence disagrees with what the active calibration snapshot currently encodes
an L1 or L0 verdict is contradicted by a human verdict on the same dimension across multiple tasks
the owner states the preference itself has changed, not that one output missed it
shared.repair: Raise a DRIFT_CANDIDATE record (class 3, automatic). Only a human activates a new calibration version (class 4) — see docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §6–§7 and AES-V2.10.

do_not.note: A single disliked output is evidence toward calibration, not license to rewrite this task's frame as if the house style itself had already changed.

text.owns: Prose execution: sentence-level clarity, rhythm, and density independent of whether the underlying argument is right, and independent of whether the language itself is correct, idiomatic, or correctly termed.
symptoms: a paragraph does not change what the reader knows or understands (constitution.md §9)
flow is uneven without any protected fact having moved
the prose is mechanically correct but empty or over-compressed
text.repair: Regenerate the affected passage. Writing-layer fixes never touch the thesis, a fact, or stated uncertainty — those are frame or verification findings.

do_not.note: Rewriting sentences does not fix a missing or wrong thesis; see the frame layer's own do_not.

Since AES-V2.17 (SUE-607), language-quality defects have their own layers: correctness routes to `normative`, unidiomatic-but-correct language to `native_fluency`, and term choice to `domain_terminology`. `writing` keeps what is left — clarity, rhythm, and density in language that is already correct and fluent. Routing a language defect here is how one "improve the prose" edit ends up changing four layers at once.

text.owns: A polish-pass regression: rhythm, connective, or word-choice change that altered a protected span, or a translationese/formulaic surface the polish pass should have caught.
symptoms: a protected span (number, date, citation, quotation, technical term) changed across a polish pass
translationese discourse scaffolding survives polish (editorial/voice.md §5, §12)
a signature rhetorical move is repeated until the house style becomes visible instead of the argument
text.repair: Re-run polish with the specific finding named. A protected-span change is always a defect, never a style choice — see `polish-invariants` (I-2, hard gate).

do_not.note: If removing a translationese pattern would require changing a protected span, polish has found a verification or terminology problem and must report it rather than silently rewrite it (editorial/voice.md, 'Protected against style-only rewrite').

A polish-shaped defect (a protected-span change, translationese, or an over-applied signature move) is not itself evidence that the thesis or argument path is wrong. Labelling it with the shared layer frame re-creates misroute 1 from the other direction: this is a prose-execution finding, not a frame finding. A genuine polish-only defect belongs at layer: null with modality_layer: "polish" — see editorial/FEEDBACK-ROUTING.md §1.

Translationese found *across a polish pass* is a polish regression and stays here. Translationese present in the draft before polish ran is a native_fluency finding. The distinction is which stage introduced it, not what it looks like.

text.owns: Content-type register mismatch: a Research piece sounds like a translated paper, a Note borrows Research's evidence cadence, or one content type's register was imported into another.
symptoms: the piece meets its profile's evidence burden but reads in the wrong register for that content type
the profile's `avoid` list is violated (editorial/profiles/content/*.json)
voice invariants are intact but the content-type-specific defaults are not
text.repair: Correct against the content-type profile's register defaults for this task. A durable register change is a content-type-profile edit — class 5, evidence-backed review.

do_not.note: A register mismatch is not evidence that the wrong reference was selected; check the profile before touching reference selection.

text.owns: Codified correctness in the output language: orthography, spacing, punctuation, standard-language form, and loanword/transliteration convention. Decided by the language's standards body, never by how often a construction appears in a reference corpus.
symptoms: a misspelling, spacing error, or wrong punctuation form against the language pack's NORMATIVE rules
a non-standard form used where the standard form is the correct one
a foreign name or term transliterated against the codified convention
the defect is present in the source language's own edited press and is still incorrect
text.repair: Correct against the language pack's NORMATIVE rule and cite the authority it derives from (editorial/profiles/language/*.json, `authority_ref`). Adding or changing a NORMATIVE rule is a language-pack edit — class 5 — and requires a standards body behind it, not corpus evidence.

do_not.note: A misspelling is not an unnaturalness finding. Correctness and fluency are different authorities and a normative defect repaired as "make the Korean more natural" leaves the error in place while rewriting prose that was fine.
Owner preference sits below NORMATIVE in the precedence order (docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §2). "The owner likes it this way" never makes an incorrect form correct.

text.owns: Prose that is correct and still not what a fluent writer of the language would produce: lexical choice and collocation, clause construction and order, subject/object handling and repetition, predicate choice, connective logic, nominalization density, and the translated-source constructions that survive a correct translation.
symptoms: every sentence is grammatical and the paragraph reads as translated rather than written
collocations are individually valid words in a combination a native writer would not reach for
connective scaffolding narrates the structure of the argument instead of making the connection (editorial/voice.md §5)
the same defect appears across genres and audiences, which is what distinguishes it from a register or audience miss
text.repair: Regenerate the affected passage against the language pack's NATIVE_QUALITY rules for this language. A durable change here requires cross-source empirical evidence and a holdout result (docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §6-7) — one awkward draft is evidence, not a rule.

do_not.note: Unidiomatic language is not a genre mismatch. Repairing it as a register change makes the piece a different genre and leaves it unidiomatic. Genre convention is the `register` layer and only applies once the language is already fluent.

Awkward language misfiled as owner preference is the specific failure SUE-607 exists to prevent: it makes a quality baseline defect look like taste, and taste is the one layer the owner is expected to arbitrate.
Fluency evidence is empirical and cannot establish correctness. A construction observed across many good sources is not thereby normative — see LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §6.

text.owns: Which term names the concept: the canonical term, its accepted rendering in the output language, whether the source-language form is retained, and whether an audience-facing alias still maps to the same concept.
symptoms: a technical term is rendered in a form no competent practitioner in that field uses (editorial/voice.md §1)
an English term is retained because it looks technical rather than because it is the normal professional usage
an audience-facing simplification names a different concept rather than a plainer surface form for the same one
the same concept is called two different things within one piece
text.repair: Correct against the language pack's `terminology` entry and its authority. Where no entry exists, add one citing a terminology authority — an agent may not invent a canonical rendering.

do_not.note: Choosing a plainer word for a young or novice reader is an audience adaptation and is legitimate. Choosing a word that means something else is a terminology defect. The test is whether the alias still maps to the recorded canonical concept, not how simple it is.
If the wrong term changed what the sentence claims, the finding has crossed into semantic integrity and routes to verification. Terminology owns the name of the concept, never the truth of the claim.

text.owns: Prose that is correct, fluent, in the right genre, at the right reading level, and using the right terms — and the owner still wants it different. Preference, explicitly lower authority than every dimension above it, and temporal.
symptoms: the objective language dimensions all pass and the owner says it does not sound like them
a construction the owner has repeatedly asked against, with no defect on any higher layer
a `preference` in editorial/voice.md is unmet while every `invariant` holds
text.repair: Record the preference as feedback. A durable change is a calibration version — human-activated, class 4 — never an in-place edit to voice.md on the strength of one disliked output. A single dislike is task-local and expires.

do_not.note: An owner dislike is not evidence that the language was unnatural. Routing taste into the native-fluency layer teaches the system a quality rule from one person's preference, which is exactly how a shared baseline becomes a house style.
Owner preference is not the content type's register. If the piece is in the wrong register for its content type, that is a `register` finding regardless of whether the owner also dislikes it.

visual.owns: The wrong artifact class was chosen for this intent — e.g. a thumbnail request routed as a body infographic, or vice versa.
symptoms: the artifact axis of the editorial intent does not match what was actually produced
information density or semantic load implied by the chosen artifact class does not fit the request
visual.repair: Re-route to the correct artifact profile under editorial/profiles/artifact/. This is an intake-layer error surfacing at the visual pipeline, not a renderer or brand defect.

do_not.note: A wrong artifact route is not a rendering defect; re-routing fixes it, re-rendering the same wrong route does not.

visual.owns: The visual's semantic specification does not carry the information the piece needs — wrong comparison chosen, wrong information gain, or a spec the image cannot honestly satisfy.
symptoms: the visual does not add information beyond the prose (fails the information-gain gate)
the semantic spec asks for a comparison the underlying data cannot support
the visual argument does not match the article's thesis
visual.repair: Rewrite the semantic spec before re-rendering. Cost ordering requires the semantic-spec gate to pass before image generation (§9).

do_not.note: A bad semantic spec produces a correctly-composed image of the wrong thing; fixing layout does not fix the spec.

visual.owns: Too much or too little information for the audience's glance-time budget and label-density tolerance.
symptoms: a legend is needed but absent, or present when the audience did not need one
the visual is cluttered past the audience's stated attention-context trait
acronyms are unexpanded for an audience that needed them expanded
visual.repair: Adjust density against the audience profile's visual traits for this task.

do_not.note: A density mismatch for one audience is not evidence the brand's default density should change.

visual.owns: Layout and arrangement: the composition does not clarify the semantic spec it was given, independent of brand tokens or rendering mechanics.
symptoms: the reader cannot find the load-bearing comparison at a glance
composition fragments the visual argument instead of clarifying it
the layout is correct per brand tokens but wrong for this specific comparison
visual.repair: Re-compose against the same semantic spec. A composition fix does not touch brand tokens.

do_not.note: A single bad layout is a composition finding, not evidence the house style's layout rules are wrong.

visual.owns: The house visual style itself — brand tokens, palette, type system, or the composition rules defined at the brand-profile level (editorial/profiles/brand/).
symptoms: repeated, independent evidence across multiple tasks that the brand tokens themselves misfire
an explicit owner declaration that the house visual style should change
visual.repair: A durable brand-profile change is a major profile edit: class 5, evidence-backed review. It is never justified by one render.

do_not.note: Do not fix a single bad render by editing the brand profile; fix the render.

visual.owns: A local, mechanical defect in one render — garbled text, a dropped element, a tool-specific artifact — that is not a defect in the spec, composition, or brand tokens it was given.
symptoms: one render has a mechanical defect (garbled text, cropped element) that a re-render of the same spec would not reproduce
the defect is specific to the rendering tool or model version, not to the instructions it received
visual.repair: Re-render from the same spec. If the same tool defect recurs across independent renders, that is calibration evidence for the renderer choice — still never a brand-profile change.

do_not.note: A renderer defect promoted to a brand-profile change rewrites the global visual style because of one bad render. See docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, misroute 2.

audio.owns: The spoken script's own argument or structure — not whether the recorded delivery lands it.
symptoms: the script's argument path does not match the article's thesis
the script is a read-aloud transcript of prose rather than something written to be heard
audio.repair: Rewrite the script structure against the frame. This precedes TTS per the cost ordering in §9: script L1 before TTS.

do_not.note: A structurally wrong script does not become right through better delivery.

audio.owns: Turn-taking and role assignment in a multi-voice script: who speaks, when, and whether the roles carry distinct functions.
symptoms: one role does all the work and the other is decorative
turns do not advance the argument, only alternate speakers mechanically
audio.repair: Rebalance roles against the script's argument path.

do_not.note: A dialogue-structure problem is not fixed by changing how fast the (still wrong) turns are delivered.

audio.owns: Term normalization for speech: a technical term, name, or number rendered incorrectly or ambiguously by TTS.
symptoms: a domain term or proper name is mispronounced by the TTS voice
a number or unit is read in a way that changes its meaning
audio.repair: Add or correct a pronunciation normalization entry. Recurrence across tasks for the same term is calibration evidence for the pronunciation lexicon.

do_not.note: A pronunciation defect is not a script-structure problem; do not rewrite the script to avoid a term the lexicon should handle.

audio.owns: Speed and segment length against the audience's attention-context trait.
symptoms: segments run long past the audience's stated attention budget
pace does not match the audience's assumed-knowledge trait (too fast for a beginner, padded for an expert)
audio.repair: Adjust segmentation and pace against the audience profile.

do_not.note: Pacing is a script/segmentation property, not a performance quality; do not treat one as the other's fix.

audio.owns: Performance quality of the rendered voice: tone, emphasis, and naturalness independent of what the script says.
symptoms: flat or misplaced emphasis that a correct script still reads badly
tone mismatched to content type (e.g. News read as casual Note)
audio.repair: Adjust delivery parameters for the same script and re-render.

do_not.note: A performance-quality complaint is not the same as a rendering/encoding defect; check which one is actually present before filing either.

audio.owns: A local, mechanical TTS rendering defect: dropped audio, encoding artifact, or tool-specific failure not present in the script or delivery parameters it was given.
symptoms: one rendered file has an artifact a re-render of the same script and parameters would not reproduce
the defect is specific to the TTS engine or voice model, not to the script
audio.repair: Re-render from the same script and delivery parameters.

do_not.note: A one-off render defect is not evidence the delivery parameters are wrong.

authority_matrix.description: The seven semantic write-authority classes from docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §10. Keyed by mutation meaning, never by filename — a path can be renamed and the authority must survive the rename. This is the executable form of that ladder; the ladder itself is authoritative and cited, not restated.

classes.name: task-local override
classes.durable_mutation: task-local override / draft or artifact correction
classes.repository_effect: none — lives in the intent record, expires with the task

classes.name: calibration activation
classes.durable_mutation: activation of durable owner preference — a new current calibration version
classes.repository_effect: new version file with supersedes lineage
classes.authorization: explicit human intent; clarification when ambiguous

classes.name: profile or core routing change
classes.durable_mutation: publication profile, core routing, or major profile change

classes.name: Constitution or SSOT boundary
classes.authorization: explicit human authorization + independent Reviewer approval

impossible_by_construction: A feedback record's scope enum (task_local, calibration_candidate) structurally tops out at class 3. No feedback record can express class 4, 5, or 6 by itself — those require an act outside the record (human activation, evidence-backed review, or human authorization plus independent Reviewer).

The authority ceiling is structural, not a text filter on the record: the feedback-record schema's scope enum has no value above calibration_candidate, and the ceiling is enforced at the actual mutation points — scripts/lib/calibration-core.mjs and scripts/lib/registry-core.mjs's promotion gates — never by matching keywords in the complaint's statement or rationale.

misroutes.rationale: The article stays wrong and reads better. See docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, misroute 1.
One bad render rewrites the house style. See docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, misroute 2.
The system accumulates prose rules for a lookup bug. See docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, misroute 3.
